name: Shintaro Tsuji
forbes_bio: Shintaro Tsuji is founder and honorary chairman of Sanrio, the Japanese creator of Hello Kitty.
He founded it as a gifts company in 1960 and went on to create the bestselling Hello Kitty character.
Tsuji's son Kunihiko died in 2013 and he passed the baton to his grandson Tomokuni, who is now Sanrio's CEO.
Sanrio, which operates two amusement parks in Japan, posted over $1 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through March 2025.

name: Yu De-Chao
forbes_bio: Yu De-Chao, also known as Michael Yu, is the chairman and CEO of Innovent Biologics, a China-headquartered biotech company.
Innovent went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Yu holds a PhD in molecular genetics from the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Yu had a postdoc position in pharmaceutical chemistry at the University of California San Francisco from 1993 to 1996.

name: Carlos Eduardo M. Scripilliti
forbes_bio: Carlos Eduardo M. Scripilliti is an heir to the Votorantim empire, one of Brazil's largest and oldest conglomerates with interests in aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, agriculture and cement.
He is the third generation member of the family business which was started by his grandfather, Jose Ermirio de Moraes, in 1918.
Today, the group, which traces its roots to a textile factory in Sao Paulo, operates in 20 countries.
Scripilliti's siblings, Clóvis Ermírio de Moraes and Regina Helena S. Velloso, are also billionaires; the trio inherited their fortune from their mother Maria Helena Moraes Scripilliti.
forbes_facts: Scripilliti's uncle, Antonio Ermirio ran to become governor of Sao Paulo, Brazil's richest state. He did not win. He died in 2014.

name: Ninian Mogan Lourdenadin
forbes_bio: Ninian Mogan Lourdenadin owns and runs trading conglomerate MBf Holdings, which has interests in everything from automobile dealerships to property development.
MBf Holdings' operation spans eight countries, nine industries and more than 30 companies.
Lourdenadin was a medical doctor who later became a property developer.
The low-profile tycoon runs one of the largest trading companies by sales in the South Pacific.
The bulk of his wealth comes from land holdings across Fiji, Australia, Malaysia,  Papua New Guinea  and the U.S.
forbes_facts: He was awarded two knighthoods, in 2008 and 2013, by Queen Elizabeth. The second was for contributions towards health, employment and commerce in Papua New Guinea.
MBf Holdings started in 1963. He took it private in 2013.

name: Li Xuechun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun China (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Li Xuechun is chairman and executive director of Fufeng Group, primarily a supplier of bio-fermentation products, with other interests including mining, real estate and finance.
His son, Li Guangyu, serves as executive director of the company.
Li took the company public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2007.

name: Daonapa Petampai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2025); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Daonapa Petampai gave up her bank job to start Muangthai Leasing with her husband Chuchat Petaumpai in 1992.
They grew the company into Thailand's biggest provider of loans against motorcycles with 7,000 branches and plan to increase to 9,000 branches by 2026.
The company's customers include farmers, factory workers and civil servants.
The couple took their company public in 2014 and changed its name to Muangthai Capital in 2018.

name: Peter Szulczewski
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2019-2021); Hurun Global (2020-2021); Hurun Global U40 (2020-2021); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Peter Szulczewski owns about 18% of e-commerce marketplace Wish, which connects shoppers with merchants who are mostly in China.
In December 2020, Wish raised $1.1 billion in an initial public offering that valued the company at $17 billion.
Szulczewski grew up in an apartment block in Tarchomin, a district of Warsaw, then immigrated with his family to Canada at age 11.
The computer science grad joined Google, where he helped build software that helps advertisers target people's searches.
He quit Google in 2009 to start his own software company, ContextLogic, which looked at a person's browsing to predict their interests.
In 2011 Szulczewski and college friend Danny Zhang re-launched the company as Wish.
forbes_facts: Szulczewski is an avid body builder and has been lifting weights since he was 15.
Wish invited people to make wish-lists of their favorite products before matching them with merchants in China.

name: Masaru Tange
forbes_bio: Masaru Tange founded software quality assurance and testing company Shift in 2005, after working as an engineering consultant.
It posted nearly $420 million in revenue in the fiscal year ended in November 2021.
Shift's compounded annual growth rate of sales and net profit over the past five years has been more than 50%.
The firm listed on Tokyo's JASDAQ exchange for startups in 2014 and eventually moved to the Tokyo Stock Exchange's First Section in 2019.
forbes_facts: Tange is the son of civil servants. He studied engineering at Kyoto University.
